entries.originalText: “My Son! walk before Me in truth, and in the simplicity of thy heart seek Me continually.
entries.modernizedText: “My Son! walk before Me in truth, and in the simplicity of your heart seek Me continually.

entries.originalText: He who walketh before Me in the truth shall be safe from evil assaults, and the truth shall deliver him from the wiles and slanders of the wicked.
entries.modernizedText: He who walks before Me in the truth will be safe from evil assaults, and the truth will deliver him from the wiles and slanders of the wicked.

entries.originalText: If the truth shall make thee free, thou shalt be free indeed, and shalt not care for the vain words of men.”
entries.modernizedText: If the truth makes you free, you will be free indeed, and will not care for the vain words of men.”

entries.originalText: Lord, it is true as Thou sayest; let it, I pray Thee, be so with me; let Thy truth teach me, let it keep me and preserve me safe unto the end.
entries.modernizedText: Lord, it is true as You say; let it, I pray You, be so with me; let Your truth teach me, let it keep me and preserve me safe to the end.

entries.originalText: Let it free me from all evil and inordinate affection, and I will walk before Thee in great freedom of heart.
entries.modernizedText: Let it free me from all evil and inordinate affection, and I will walk before You in great freedom of heart.

entries.originalText: “I will teach thee,” saith the Truth, “the things which are right and pleasing before Me.
entries.modernizedText: “I will teach you,” says the Truth, “the things that are right and pleasing before Me.

entries.originalText: Think upon thy sins with great displeasure and sorrow, and never think thyself anything because of thy good works.
entries.modernizedText: Think of your sins with great displeasure and sorrow, and never think yourself anything because of your good works.

entries.originalText: Verily thou art a sinner, liable to many passions, yea, tied and bound with them.
entries.modernizedText: Truly you are a sinner, liable to many passions, indeed tied and bound with them.

entries.originalText: Of thyself thou always tendest unto nothing, thou wilt quickly fall, quickly be conquered, quickly disturbed, quickly undone.
entries.modernizedText: Of yourself you always tend toward nothing; you will quickly fall, quickly be conquered, quickly disturbed, quickly undone.

entries.originalText: Thou hast nought whereof to glory, but many reasons why thou shouldest reckon thyself vile, for thou art far weaker than thou art able to comprehend.
entries.modernizedText: You have nothing to glory in, but many reasons to consider yourself vile, for you are far weaker than you are able to comprehend.

entries.originalText: “Let, therefore, nothing which thou doest seem to thee great; let nothing be grand, nothing of value or beauty, nothing worthy of honour, nothing lofty, nothing praiseworthy or desirable, save what is eternal.
entries.modernizedText: “Therefore let nothing you do seem great to you; let nothing be grand, nothing of value or beauty, nothing worthy of honor, nothing lofty, nothing praiseworthy or desirable, except what is eternal.

entries.originalText: Let the eternal truth please thee above all things, let thine own great vileness displease thee continually.
entries.modernizedText: Let the eternal truth please you above all things; let your own great vileness displease you continually.

entries.originalText: Fear, denounce, flee nothing so much as thine own faults and sins, which ought to be more displeasing to thee than any loss whatsoever of goods.
entries.modernizedText: Fear, denounce, and flee nothing so much as your own faults and sins, which ought to be more displeasing to you than any loss whatsoever of goods.

entries.originalText: There are some who walk not sincerely before me, but being led by curiosity and pride, they desire to know my secret things and to understand the deep things of God, whilst they neglect themselves and their salvation.
entries.modernizedText: There are some who do not walk sincerely before Me, but, led by curiosity and pride, desire to know My secret things and to understand the deep things of God, while they neglect themselves and their salvation.

entries.originalText: These often fall into great temptations and sins because of their pride and curiosity, for I am against them.
entries.modernizedText: These often fall into great temptations and sins because of their pride and curiosity, for I am against them.

entries.originalText: “Fear thou the judgments of God, fear greatly the wrath of the Almighty.
entries.modernizedText: “Fear the judgments of God; greatly fear the wrath of the Almighty.

entries.originalText: Shrink from debating upon the works of the Most High, but search narrowly thine own iniquities into what great sins thou hast fallen, and how many good things thou hast neglected.
entries.modernizedText: Shrink from debating the works of the Most High, but closely examine your own iniquities, into what great sins you have fallen, and how many good things you have neglected.

entries.originalText: There are some who carry their devotion only in books, some in pictures, some in outward signs and figures; some have Me in their mouths, but little in their hearts.
entries.modernizedText: There are some who carry their devotion only in books, some in pictures, some in outward signs and figures; some have Me in their mouths, but little in their hearts.

entries.originalText: Others there are who, being enlightened in their understanding and purged in their affections, continually long after eternal things, hear of earthly things with unwillingness, obey the necessities of nature with sorrow.
entries.modernizedText: There are others who, being enlightened in their understanding and purged in their affections, continually long for eternal things, hear of earthly things unwillingly, and obey the necessities of nature with sorrow.

entries.originalText: And these understand what the Spirit of truth speaketh in them; for He teacheth them to despise earthly things and to love heavenly; to neglect the world and to desire heaven all the day and night.”
entries.modernizedText: And these understand what the Spirit of truth speaks in them; for He teaches them to despise earthly things and to love heavenly things; to neglect the world and to desire heaven all day and night.”
